messages:
Emily Chen: Quick follow-up to the tenant credential separation RFC — we saw a couple of small customer audits that flagged potential token leakage across org boundaries. I want us to list low-effort mitigations and one medium-term refactor we can prioritize.
Raj Patel: Yep, saw that too. Short term: enforce tenant-id binding in token introspection and add a runtime check in the proxy layer.
Sasha Rivera: Agree. Also throttle any cross-tenant token exchange attempts and alert on them.
Leon Müller: For clarification, by 'token introspection' you mean our authn gateway validating `tenant_id` claim against the requested resource's org?
Emily Chen: Exactly. And if the token doesn't match the resource's org, return 403 and include cross-tenant alert flag to telemetry.
Raj Patel: Minimal change: patch gateway to check claim + add a metric `auth.cross_tenant_rejects`. Medium-term: split service actor keys vs project keys so operators can't accidentally use project API keys for cross-tenant operations.
Sasha Rivera: On the split keys idea — it's a decent security win but has UX impact. Customers that pinned service workflows will need migration tooling. We should propose an automated migration path (shadow-check, migration report).
Leon Müller: Migration plan idea: start with shadow-enforcement mode (log-only), then opt-in blocking, then gradual enforcement with a one-click migrate that rotates keys to scoped tokens.
Emily Chen: I like that. Also consider ephemeral tokens for automation workflows: short TTL + mint-on-demand using operator identity. Cuts blast radius on leaked tokens.
Raj Patel: Tradeoffs: ephemeral tokens increase latency for cold minting. We can mitigate with a local cache and pre-warming for common scheduled jobs.
Sasha Rivera: Operational note: make sure audit logs include the minting principal and the parent token id so we can trace back (customer asks for that frequently in audits).
Leon Müller: For RBAC enforcement, do we want to keep using policy engine X as-is or move to an attribute-based policy (ABAC) that includes `tenant_id` as a first-class attribute?
Emily Chen: Short answer: leave X for now but add a `tenant_id` guard in the admission point. Long-term, ABAC seems cleaner for complex cross-tenant rules. Put ABAC on the roadmap for Q3 refactor.
Raj Patel: Action items: 1) Patch gateway check + metric (priority: P0), 2) Add shadow-mode cross-tenant logging (P1), 3) Design key-surface split + migration RFC (P1), 4) Add ephemeral-token pilot for scheduled jobs (P2), 5) Roadmap ABAC refactor (Q3).
Sasha Rivera: I'm happy to own the shadow-mode logging + metric work. Will open a PR with log format and sample dashboards.
Leon Müller: I'll prototype the shadow enforcement flow and one-click rotate UX for the console.
Emily Chen: I'll draft the migration RFC for the key-surface split — include cost/UX estimates and sample CLI flow.
InfraBot: DeployBot: new auth-gateway patch candidate available in staging: `auth-gw:tenant-guard:v2028-rc1` — run integration tests before canary. :robot_face:
Raj Patel: Thanks InfraBot — I'll run the integration tests today and report failures to this thread.
Sasha Rivera: Small note: include a s3-presigned-token example in the RFC appendix showing how tenant binding is preserved for third-party uploads.
Emily Chen: Good call. Also add a snippet for `token_introspect` response with `tenant_id` field documented.
Leon Müller: Sounds solid. If no objections, we'll ship the gateway check as hotfix and start shadow-mode next sprint.
Emily Chen: No objections from me. Marking this thread as the working thread for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
